Title: Viral podcast recounts 2016 drug trafficking case, says KL police chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The drug trafficking case near a place of worship close to the Sentul district police headquarters, recounted in the @Sembangohhyeahh podcast, dates back to 2016.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said three police reports were lodged in connection with the case on July 12, 2016.
Fadil said police detected a video from the podcast that went viral this morning.
The video featured a journalist recounting an undercover assignment to expose drug trafficking activities in the area, while claiming that no action had been taken.
"Based on further checks, the podcast content was a retelling of a guest's journalism experience that occurred in 2016," he said in a statement today.
He said such publicity was unwarranted as it could create a negative public perception of the police and affect the force's image and credibility.
He added that all parties must exercise greater care and responsibility when sharing or disseminating information to the public.
"The police are committed to continuously preserving integrity and public trust in the policing institution for the safety and well-being of the nation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH candidates must build strong campaign machinery - Ramanan
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates contesting the Nov 14 Melaka state election must build strong campaign machinery rather than rely solely on their track records in serving the community to win voter support, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said.
He said a strong record in looking after the people's welfare would not be enough if candidates lacked a capable team to mobilise an effective campaign.
Ramanan said a solid campaign team was essential to help candidates reach voters in different locations, as they could not be everywhere at the same time.
"This is my personal view: candidates need strong campaign machinery. During a campaign, we cannot be in 10 places at the same time.
"So candidates must start building large, capable teams to help drive their campaigns at various locations," he told reporters after attending the HRD Corp Pocket Talk Roadshow programme, themed 'Dari Dasar ke Rakyat' (From Policy to the People) today.
The programme was also attended by HRD Corp chief executive Datuk Shamir Aziz.
The Sungai Buloh MP said candidates needed to move away from the old approach of relying solely on their own efforts without building a support team, and instead adapt to the challenges of today's political landscape.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also stressed the importance of selecting candidates who actively engaged with the people, worked on the ground and enjoyed public acceptance.
Ramanan said PH's candidate selection process also took credibility into account, including through stringent vetting involving criminal record checks and assessments of candidates' financial standing to ensure they met the stipulated criteria.
Oct 31 has been set for
nominations
, while early voting is on Nov 10.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while PH secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Sharafuddin's 25-year reign reflects deep concern for people's welfare, unity
Article:
KLANG: The 25-year reign of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has been marked by his concern for the welfare of his subjects, the interests of Islam and harmony among the state's multi-ethnic communities.
This was the sentiment expressed by attendees at a Royal Tea Reception with the People held at Istana Alam Shah today in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of the Sultan's reign.
They said His Royal Highness's attentiveness to the concerns of the people was an important foundation for safeguarding their well-being and strengthening unity in the state.
[[nid:1558387]]
Bagan Nira village head Mohamad Sedek Idrus said Sultan Sharafuddin's firm stance on state issues, particularly those concerning Islam, reflected his commitment to fulfilling his responsibilities as ruler.
Sedek, who hails from Sabak Bernam, said that while the Sultan consistently upheld the interests of Islam, he also respected the rights of other communities and emphasised unity in his public statements.
"On behalf of the villagers, I would like to express my gratitude to His Royal Highness the Sultan of Selangor. He is a ruler who truly cares for his people, ensuring that they can live well and enjoy the state's prosperity," he told Bernama at the event.
Meanwhile, private university student Nur Aresha Zaraa Sallehudin, 21, described the royal institution as an important part of the nation's identity that society should respect and cherish.
She likened the institution to roots that bind society under a common leadership, thereby strengthening unity and benefiting the country.
"Much like the proverb 'united we stand, divided we fall', the royal institution serves as these roots, further strengthening unity and bringing other benefits, including economic progress," she said.
Nur Aresha also prayed for Sultan Sharafuddin's continued good health and prosperity so that His Royal Highness could continue to rule the state with integrity and efficiency.
Earlier, Sultan Sharafuddin, accompanied by the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, graced the reception, which was attended by more than 3,000 people from the districts of Klang, Petaling, Hulu Selangor and Sabak Bernam.
Also in attendance were the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah, and his wife, Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz.
The reception was the first of five events organised to celebrate the Silver Jubilee of the Sultan's reign.
Upon their arrival, the royal couple and other members of the royal family were welcomed by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and state secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin.
In his address, Fadzli said Sultan Sharafuddin's leadership was distinguished by his genuine concern for the grievances of people at the grassroots level, extending beyond discussions in meeting rooms and royal decrees issued from the palace.
He said the Sultan's decrees, guidance and admonitions, whether delivered in the state legislative assembly, at Royal Council meetings or from mosque pulpits, served as guiding principles in formulating state government policies.
"When His Royal Highness speaks on the importance of transparent financial management, the state government immediately strengthens its procurement governance. When His Royal Highness addresses environmental sustainability, the state government reviews its forestry and flood mitigation policies.
"When His Royal Highness firmly highlights the dangers of corruption and misappropriation, it becomes the absolute duty of myself, in my capacity as the state secretary, and all heads of departments to ensure that no leakage of public funds occurs in Selangor," he said.
Fadzli said the state administration's commitment to upholding the Sultan's decrees and advice demonstrated its loyalty to the royal institution.
"I firmly hold to the principle that an excellent administration is not merely one that excels in planning, but one that is also adept at executing those plans transparently, for the well-being of the people who reside under His Highness's care," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno Youth pledges mature, healthy conduct in Melaka polls
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Umno Youth has pledged to maintain mature, healthy and professional political conduct throughout the upcoming Melaka election.
Its election director, Mohd Hairi Mad Shah, said the party would adopt a positive campaigning approach.
He said the youth campaign machinery would highlight BN's record in government from 1957 to 2018.
"BN does not engage in speculation or slander. Instead, we want to share the positive things so that the people can see and judge for themselves," he said.
Mohd Hairi, who is also Umno Youth deputy chief, said the party's youth machinery across all 191 divisions nationwide would be mobilised to support the Melaka election campaign.
He said the state campaign teams, including Umno Youth executive council members and division leaders, had been assigned their respective tasks.
The party would engage with communities and voters in Melaka in an effort to maintain the winning momentum from Johor and Negri Sembilan, he said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka election, with nomination day scheduled for Oct 31.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants in haze-affected states can opt for hybrid WFH arrangement
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Civil servants working in states affected by the transboundary haze may carry out their duties under the Hybrid Working Day (HBH) policy.
Public Service Department director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the haze problem coincided with the government's introduction of the HBH policy, which came into effect on Aug 1.
He said department heads, particularly in states affected by haze, were allowed to implement the HBH arrangement.
"Department heads must set key performance indicators (KPIs) to ensure civil servants' productivity remains a priority even when they work from home under the hybrid arrangement," he said.
Earlier, Wan Ahmad Dahlan conducted a Retiree Outreach Programme, visiting and spending time with three retirees here.
Also present was state Federal Development Department director, Datuk Abdul Kahar Abdul Latif.
Under the HBH arrangement, civil servants work physically in the office for three days a week, while the remaining two days are spent working from home or at an approved alternative location.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan called on all civil servants, particularly those serving in haze-affected states, to wear face masks to protect themselves against haze-related health risks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri MB on Tuanku Muhriz's rebuke: 'There's nothing to comment'
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declined to elaborate on the viral video which showed Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, having a stern word with him at a Kuala Pilah mosque last Friday.
The Juasseh assemblyman, when met by reporters, only offered a smile and said he was doing well.
"I'm okay. There's nothing to comment," he replied briefly to reporters' questions when met after the launch of the Negri Sembilan Antlers Sepak Takraw team here.
A video showing Tuanku Muhriz having a stern word with Ismail amid the state's constitutional crisis went viral last week.
In the clip,
Tuanku Muhriz is heard telling Ismail
that he does not want to see him.
The ruler is also heard expressing his dissatisfaction with Ismail and former state executive council members over a letter to the Keeper of the Rulers' Seal stating that he was no longer the state ruler.
Ismail is seen in the clip acknowledging Tuanku Muhriz and paying homage to the ruler.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the state assembly sitting has been set for Nov 26 and remains unchanged, following its postponement on Oct 16.
"As of now, it's still the same. There have been no changes. Preparations are going smoothly," he said.
Last Friday, 11 Negri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan assemblymen had called on the state government to call for the state assembly to be convened.
State opposition chief, J Arul Kumar, said checks at the e-Dewan portal showed that the proceedings were still slated for five days from Oct 16 to 22, 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Undi18, automatic voter registration a challenge for BN in Melaka polls
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: The implementation of 'Undi18' and the automatic voter registration system pose a challenge for Barisan Nasional (BN) in the upcoming Melaka state election, which will take place next month.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said therefore the BN machinery must strengthen its strategies to engage these new voters moving beyond reliance on traditional methods alone to ensure that support for the party is maintained.
"In the past, we could register voters, collect their names, and keep them in our own 'basket. We could gauge whether we would win if we contested in a particular area. However, with the inclusion of new voters which encompasses not only those aged 18 but also people aged 60 and above who had never voted before the situation changed.
"We didn't know who these people were or where they came from, as they were registered as voters automatically... in the end, we lost the Alor Gajah parliamentary seat," he said while officiating the launch of the Barisan Nasional (BN) election machinery for the Alor Gajah parliamentary constituency at Dewan Kampung Permai, Machap Umboo, today.
The Melaka BN chairman noted that although the coalition secured a resounding victory in the 2021 Melaka state election, this success could not be replicated during the 15th general election (GE15), where the coalition lost all six parliamentary seats.
The Election Commission (EC) had previously set the polling day for the Melaka State Election for Nov 14, with candidate nominations on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 out of the 28 contested seats, enabling it to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cat Stevens offers comfort to grieving Dr Mahathir
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A visit by legendary singer-songwriter Yusuf Islam, better known as Cat Stevens, to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad following the death of his wife,
Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali
, has touched Malaysians, with many praising the musician for offering comfort during a difficult time.
Yusuf shared that he had visited Dr Mahathir, whose wife died recently after 70 years of marriage.
"Today I visited Dr Mahathir Mohamad, former prime minister of Malaysia, whose wife, Dr Hasmah, just passed away and read Al-Fatihah. They were married for 70 years. He is 101 years old, by God's grace," he wrote in a Facebook post.
The post featured a photograph of Yusuf sitting beside Dr Mahathir, with the two men engaged in conversation in what appeared to be a quiet, personal moment.
The visit drew an emotional response from Malaysians and other social media users, many of whom thanked the singer for taking the time to visit the veteran statesman as he mourned the loss of his wife.
Among those who commented was Diana Able, who thanked Yusuf for visiting Dr Mahathir during his time of grief.
"Thank you for taking the time to visit this individual who is experiencing extreme grief due to the loss of his wife," she wrote.
"Sitting beside someone during grief is the greatest gift we can give to them."
Another commenter, Hamzah Mat Isa, described Dr Mahathir as a politician who had helped build Malaysia through years of challenges. He added that the veteran leader would appreciate the visit, having grown up listening to Yusuf's music.
"You are quite famous in Malaysia too," he added.
The photograph also struck an emotional chord with social media user Zul Daud, who said he was deeply moved by the gesture.
"Thank you, Cat Stevens, for taking the time to meet with our country's great leader. I do not know why, but tears welled up in my eyes after writing this post," he wrote.
Others offered prayers and expressed appreciation for Yusuf's kindness, while some reflected on the significance of the encounter between the internationally renowned musician and Malaysia's veteran leader.
One commenter also praised the visit as a reminder of the importance of companionship and compassion for elderly people, particularly those grieving the loss of a lifelong partner.
"Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah were married for 70 years, making their relationship one of Malaysia's most enduring public partnerships," the commenter wrote.
Yusuf, 78, rose to international fame in the 1960s and 1970s under the name Cat Stevens, with songs such as 'Father and Son', 'Wild World' and 'Morning Has Broken'.
He later embraced Islam and adopted the name Yusuf Islam in 1977.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2 held in Rawang subsidised diesel bust
Article:
RAWANG: Two men were arrested after authorities seized 11,900 litres of subsidised diesel allegedly diverted through the misuse of fleet cards at an illegal storage facility in Rawang.
Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Muhamad Hanif Asa'ari said the raid was conducted under Ops Tiris 4.0.
He said the storage facility was raided following intelligence gathering and the detection of suspected subsidised diesel diversion in the area.
The suspects, aged 29 and 68, are believed to have worked as the facility's caretaker and a tanker lorry driver respectively.
Muhamad Hanif said investigations found that the syndicate bought subsidised diesel at nearby petrol stations using fleet cards under the Subsidised Diesel Control System 2.0 before transferring it to buyers.
The seized items included 11,900 litres of subsidised diesel, a tanker lorry, a bonded lorry, 12 intermediate bulk containers, three sets of rubber hoses and a pump machine. Their total value was estimated at RM82,482.
He said drivers bought subsidised diesel at several nearby petrol stations using fleet cards and transferred it directly into buyers' lorries.
The diesel was also stored at the illegal facility in Rawang before being pumped into tanker lorries for delivery and sale to industrial operators or other buyers, he said.
Muhamad Hanif said an investigation paper had been opened under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 (Act 122) to identify the individuals or companies involved and trace the suspected diesel distribution network.
He warned companies and other parties against misusing the fleet cards.
Those found guilty could face action under Act 122, including fines of up to RM3 million and imprisonment for individuals, he said.
Companies and statutory bodies could face fines of up to RM5 million for repeat offences and could also be investigated under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC, EC test internet connectivity at Melaka polling centres for OCR-VA system
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Election Commission (EC) have conducted internet connectivity checks at polling centres to test the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system ahead of the Melaka state election, which will take place next month.
State Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications Committee chairman Datuk Fairul Nizam Roslan said one polling centre, Dewan Penyayang at the Lesung Batu Welfare Complex, was found to be unsuitable for the OCR-VA system due to unsatisfactory internet connectivity.
"As such, the polling centre will be relocated to the Machap Baru State Constituency Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) Complex," he said after the launch of the Barisan Nasional (BN) election machinery for the Alor Gajah parliamentary constituency at Dewan Kampung Permai in Machap Umboo today.
The event was officiated by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Fairul Nizam said MCMC had also submitted a full report to the EC on internet connectivity at the polling centres to facilitate arrangements on election day.
"I am confident that the EC is fully prepared to use the system on polling day, with assistance from the MCMC," he said.
It was earlier reported that the OCR-VA system would be used more extensively in the upcoming Melaka state election to automatically record and mark voters' attendance by scanning information on their identification documents.
The system is expected to expedite attendance verification and recording, reduce errors in manual marking, and improve the efficiency of polling staff and the voting process on election day.
A pilot project for the system was introduced during the Negri Sembilan state election in August this year.
The EC has set
Nov 14
as polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pejuang eyes up to 3 seats in Melaka polls
Article:
IPOH: Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) is eyeing two to three seats in the upcoming Melaka state election.
Its president, Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, said informal discussions among Perikatan Nasional (PN) component parties had begun ahead of the Nov 14 polls.
"We hope to reach an agreement with the other parties for Pejuang to field candidates.
"Two or three seats would be enough. If we get one or two, we are fine with that," he told reporters after officiating the Perak Pejuang Convention at Hotel Seri Malaysia today.
Mukhriz said Pejuang would campaign alongside its coalition partners.
"In Negeri Sembilan, we continued working with our PN partners even though we did not contest. We hope the same cooperation will continue in Melaka," he said.
Pejuang did not field any candidates in the August Negeri Sembilan state election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nurse dies after 4WD plunges into river in Ranau
Article:
RANAU: A nurse died after the four-wheel-drive vehicle she was driving plunged about 30m into a river near Kampung Nalapak, along Jalan Ranau-Telupid.
Nancy Kitingon, 47, was pronounced dead at the scene.
Ranau district police chief Superintendent Mursalin Mahmud said the victim was driving an Isuzu D-Max from Telupid when the vehicle hit the barrier on the left side of a bridge before plunging into the river.
"The vehicle is believed to have overturned," he said when contacted.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Earlier, seven firefighters and two fire engines from the Ranau Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the crash site.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saudi landmark closes offices after repeated Houthi attacks
Article:
RIYADH: Riyadh's Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordered remote working for office tenants on Sunday following repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The imposing, 99-storey landmark announced "mandatory" remote working until further notice.
No reason was given for the order, but it comes a week after 13 people were killed in a major Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport.
The Saudi coalition's decade-plus war with the Iran-backed Houthis has reignited during the US-Iran war, with regular attacks reported by both sides.
Tenants of the Kingdom Centre, which towers over central Riyadh, include financial services giant Merril Lynch, management consultancy McKinsey and the International Monetary Fund.
"Please be advised that remote working arrangements are mandatory for all office employees at Kingdom Centre, effective immediately and until further notice," the building's management said in an email seen by AFP.
"Kindly refrain from attending the offices during this period," it added. The mall at the foot of the building remains open.
It comes as schools recently extended remote learning measures and Riyadh's airport remains closed after last week's attack.
The order came after the coalition announced the death of two helicopter pilots in Najran near the border with Yemen, blaming a "technical malfunction", after the Houthis said they shot down an Apache helicopter in the area.
Late on Saturday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.
After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen's conflict has surged back to life and intensified when the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis have hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh's King Khalid International airport.
The Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government has launched repeated air raids on Houthi territory.
The coalition said overnight it intercepted two drones in the Riyadh area and a third over the oil-rich Eastern Province. Saudi authorities had earlier issued a threat alert in the capital.
The coalition also said two ballistic missiles were intercepted in the kingdom's south.
On Saturday, the Houthis reported that Saudi strikes killed 12 people in Yemen, including three children.
The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and captured territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf's Strait of Hormuz.
The Red Sea is a key shipping route, connecting Asia with Europe via Egypt's Suez Canal.
On Sunday, Egypt's parliament will hold an emergency session after President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi asked lawmakers to authorise support to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.
Sisi said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.
"I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," he said on Saturday. "We are speaking only about defence."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11.4pct figure does not reflect actual progress of Sabah Pan Borneo Highway - Dr Joachim
Article:
KUDAT: The 11.4 per cent completion rate for the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project highlighted in the recent Auditor-General's Report does not reflect the actual physical progress on the ground, says Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam.
The Sabah Public Works Minister said the figure only measured the number of fully handed-over packages, which accounted for just four of the 35 packages under Phase 1 of the project.
"Although the 11.4 per cent figure is correct in terms of handed-over packages, it does not reflect overall progress as other packages are actively being built, with some alignments recording between 90 and 93 per cent physical progress," he told reporters on the sidelines of the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah convention here today.
He said construction works continued to show positive progress, with eight packages spanning 179 kilometres (km) proposed to be opened to motorists in stages before the end of 2026.
On the variation order (VO) issue, reported to have exceeded RM514 million, Dr Joachim clarified that the approval for the additional cost falls under the jurisdiction of the federal Works Ministry and Finance Ministry, not the state government.
He said the Sabah Public Works Department (JKR) only acts as the technical implementing agency and has no authority to approve the VO.
According to Dr Joachim, the VO was necessitated by actual technical factors, such as Sabah's unpredictable hilly topography, which involves slope stability issues, as well as swampy and peat soil structures that change every one to 1.5 km.
"The state government views the audit findings positively and has taken steps to address them, supported by the excellent cooperation between the state and federal governments," he said.
Commenting on project delays, Dr Joachim said the implementation of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway was affected by the termination of the previous project delivery partner (PDP) model, which forced a shift to the conventional method, making the project reliant on annual federal allocation approvals.
In addition to the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021, most contractor appointments for new packages could only be finalised between February 2024 and January 2026 after the federal government reconsidered the implementation method.
He added that delays also stemmed from a time-consuming land acquisition process.
He explained that the government did not take a draconian approach but instead allowed landowners to appeal for compensation, while also acknowledging challenges related to the performance of some contractors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GRS needs to priorities Sabah, coalition over personal interests - Hajiji
Article:
KUDAT: All component parties of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) must prioritise the interests of Sabah and the coalition over personal or individual party interests, in order to strengthen the state's bargaining power at the federal level, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
The Sabah chief minister said the state's political leverage in negotiations at the federal level must be anchored in the internal cohesion of GRS, rather than being undermined by power struggles for positions or political egos.
"There is no point in praising the unity of others if we are still bickering within the GRS fold itself; for the true strength of Sabah begins with our own unity.
"No (component) party is so large that it no longer needs its partners, and no party is so small that its contributions can be dismissed," he said while delivering the keynote address at the 2026 GRS Convention at Dewan Tun Mustapha today.
Also present were GRS deputy chairmen Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, Tan Sri Anifah Aman, Tan Sri Liew Yun Fah, Datuk Ewon Benedick, and Datuk Chin Su Phin, as well as GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
Hajiji also expressed his appreciation to the grassroots members who sacrificed their time, energy, and personal funds to campaign during elections, while reminding leaders not to forget their contributions once they have attained power.
He said the decision by certain parties to leave the coalition and go it alone should serve as a lesson one that helps mature the decision-making process and strengthens the foundational principles upon which GRS was established in 2020, all for the sake of the state's stability.
He emphasised that merely being a local-based party is not enough to win the confidence of voters if the government fails to address the people's daily challenges or provide economic opportunities.
"The people want a stable government, one that does more than just talk well, it must be capable of solving problems. We might win the battle of speeches on stage, yet still fail to win the hearts of the people," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MEF calls for study before mandatory RM2,500 graduate salary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called for a thorough study before the government makes a minimum starting salary for graduates mandatory.
Its president, Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman, said salary requirements varied across industries depending on the skills and knowledge required for different professions.
"While some basic knowledge can be the same, the details of the professions require different skills and knowledge.
"Industries may have different entry-level salary points to suit their respective requirements.
"A one-size-fits-all recommendation may be risky and not applicable," he said when contacted.
He was commenting on the government's plan to amend the National Wages Consultative Council Act to compel employers to
pay graduates a minimum
starting salary of RM2,500.
Syed Hussain said hiring decisions went beyond academic qualifications, with employers also assessing candidates' communication, teamwork, presentation and analytical skills.
"We must also not be in a position where we cannot decide the starting salary based on the strength of the candidate.
"MEF has no objections to any studies, but it is the execution that we are worried about," he said.
Syed Hussain said businesses were already struggling with supply chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions, rising costs, margin compression, higher interest rates, higher statutory deductions and delayed payments.
He added that the recent minimum wage increase was about 18 per cent higher, and many employers were still struggling with the RM1,700 rate before it rises to RM2,000.
"Any additional cost increase may not be the right time.
"We must learn to phase things for better success. It's all about timing the implementation, not agenda ticking," he said.
Syed Hussain said MEF remained open to collective discussions to address issues, for industrial harmony and acceptance by all stakeholders.
The Human Resources Ministry will introduce guidelines on
starting salaries for graduates and semi-skilled workers
by June 2027, following the government's announcement of a proposed RM2,500 minimum starting salary under Budget 2027.
Its minister, Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, said the guidelines would provide employers and workers with a reference for basic starting salaries based on occupations, educational qualifications and skills.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schools in Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, Penang to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MOE) in Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, and Penang will reopen and resume normal operations tomorrow.
In
SELANGOR,
the state Education Department said that outdoor activities are to be suspended, and students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks.
School administrators are required to continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and pay special attention to high-risk students.
"Parents or guardians who are concerned about their children's health may choose not to send them to school, provided that they notify the school," the statement read.
The Selangor Education Department also advised all relevant parties to rely solely on official channels or the schools themselves to obtain accurate and up-to-date information.
In
NEGRI SEMBILAN,
the state Education Department has announced that the End-of-Academic-Session Examinations (UASA) scheduled for this period must be postponed and rescheduled by the respective schools, in light of the haze currently affecting the country.
"This directive also applies to all internal examinations conducted by the schools. All outdoor activities must be halted if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100," the statement read.
In
MELAKA,
the state Education Department said that school administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings provided by the Department of Environment (DOE) and pay special attention to high-risk students.
The department also advised parents, guardians, and the school community to regularly check official communication channels, either the Melaka state education or the respective schools, to obtain accurate and up-to-date information.
Meanwhile, in
PAHANG
, the state Education Department said that all schools in the Bentong district will continue to operate as usual. However, all outdoor activities are to be postponed until further notice.
All schools in other districts are operating as usual.
"Any changes regarding school operations will be announced through the official channels of the Pahang state Education Department (Pahang) and the respective district education offices," the statement added.
A similar situation was also reported in Penang, where the Penang Education Department issued a statement encouraging students to wear face masks and stay well-hydrated, while also requesting that schools ensure an adequate supply of drinking water.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tawau fire victims thank PM for contribution
Article:
TAWAU: Victims of the fire at Batu 2, Jalan Apas, have expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the special assistance provided to help ease the burden on affected families.
Mohd Azmi Mohd Asri, 24, said the contribution from the prime minister was deeply appreciated and reflected his concern for the tragedy that had befallen the villagers.
He recounted that he was out delivering food when a friend informed him that a
fire
had broken out near his home.
"I rushed home and saw a large fire coming from a neighbour's house behind mine. I managed to salvage some items from the refrigerator, a few pieces of clothing and personal documents. My parents had already escaped by then.
"I am grateful that everyone is safe. I hope to receive government assistance to repair my fire-damaged home," he said when met at a special assistance presentation ceremony initiated by the prime minister and delivered by Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud today at the temporary evacuation centre at the Tawau Sports Complex multipurpose hall.
Villager Abdul Japar Judin, 56, also thanked the prime minister for the assistance provided to ease the burden on the victims and acknowledged the non-governmental organisations that had offered help following the incident.
Abdul Japar, a teacher at St Patrick's Primary School, said he never expected his own home to be destroyed in the fire, which broke out at 9.31pm. However, he was thankful that he had managed to ensure his family members reached safety.
He suggested that villagers be given more frequent exposure to fire safety awareness programmes, particularly on initial firefighting efforts.
Such knowledge could help reduce the risk of large-scale fires, especially as the houses were estimated to be just one metre apart.
Earlier, Mustapha presented assistance to 69 heads of households affected by the fire. He expressed his condolences to the victims and hoped the aid would help ease their burden.
He said further assistance was expected from other sources, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the state government.
He also reminded the public to be more vigilant at home, particularly when using kitchen equipment and electrical appliances, to reduce the risk of fires, especially during hot weather.
"Thank you to the prime minister. He is a truly caring person."
He said the 2027 Budget had increased the allocation for Nadma to RM260 million, including an increase in home repair assistance for disaster victims, such as those affected by fires, from RM5,000 to RM10,000.
In the incident, 15 houses were destroyed by fire, affecting 267 people from 69 households.

Title: Oregon families grapple with explaining school shooting to children
Article:
LIZ'S seven-year-old-nephew hasn't been able to sleep since a teenage shooter opened fire at his Oregon elementary school, killing three children and a teacher.
"He kept hearing the sound of gunshots" ringing through his head, even as his parents spent all of Thursday night comforting the Silver Rail Elementary pupil, she told AFP.
Parents and caregivers in this city, known for its mountain skyline and outdoor activities, are reeling from the tragedy and searching for ways to discuss what happened with their children.
Sixteen-year-old Griffin John II killed three children and a teacher in the same special needs class he previously attended, before a father who happened to be passing the school grabbed his own gun and killed the attacker, authorities said.
Another student, a seven-year-old girl, and another teacher were wounded, but are in stable condition.
Communication is crucial after such an event, local pediatrician Logan Clausen told CNN.
"Talk to them about what they know, talk to them about what they're feeling. You can gently correct inaccurate facts," the doctor said.
Dozens of people gathered on a street in Bend, many accompanied by children of various ages, to hold a vigil late on Friday.
Jeff Michaels, a father of three, told AFP that he and his wife have let their children know it is OK to talk about what happened and ask questions.
"We want to know how they feel, and they do ask questions," he said, hugging one of his daughters. "They want to know why this happened, why people are sad."
The challenge of helping little ones process the trauma is acute for caregivers of children with special needs.
[[nid:1558317]]
Since the Thursday rampage, Sherry Lauer, 56, has been watching her five-year-old granddaughter for signs of how she is processing the tragedy.
"She's nonverbal, so we're not sure how much she is comprehending about what is going on at the moment," Lauer told AFP.
While the little girl is not a student at Silver Rail, she "stopped what she was doing and paid attention" to a news conference about the school shooting.
So far, the girl has not shown any negative reactions, her grandmother added.
Art centres, restaurants and parks in Bend, a city of around 100,000 people in central Oregon through which the Deschutes River winds, opened their doors and organized special activities for children over the weekend.
"My mom's been crying a lot, and I'm sad too," an eight-year-old girl who attended the Friday vigil with her aunt told AFP.
The girl attends another school, but when news alerts about the shooting began circulating, her mother picked her up and took her home, where she explained what had happened.
The aunt, who asked not to be identified, said her sister has been encouraging the girl "to just ask questions and just answering them as they come up."
"She kept saying she missed me so much after it happened," the child said.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Pasir Gudang tops unhealthy air quality readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-six areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, with Pasir Gudang, Johor, registering the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 181.
The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System portal showed Kota Tinggi recording the second-highest reading at 178.
Nilai in Negeri Sembilan recorded 169, followed by Larkin in Johor at 168.
Seremban and Pengerang both recorded readings of 167, while Bukit Rambai in Melaka registered 166 and Batu Pahat recorded 165.
Kluang in Johor and Johan Setia in Selangor both recorded readings of 161, followed by Bandaraya Melaka at 159 and Alor Gajah at 158.
Tangkak and Segamat recorded readings of 158 and 156 respectively.
Putrajaya, Petaling Jaya and Shah Alam, as well as Kuching and Serian each recorded readings of 155.
Rompin in Pahang recorded 154, while Batu Muda and Cheras in Kuala Lumpur, and Klang, registered 153.
Port Dickson recorded 152, followed by Banting at 151.
Samarahan in Sarawak recorded the lowest reading among the 26 areas, at 132.
A further 41 areas recorded moderate air quality, while Balik Pulau in Penang was the only area with good air quality, at 42.
Readings of 0 to 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.

Title: Tighter border controls curb drug supplies into Kelantan, says police chief
Article:
KOTA BARU: Drug supplies into Kelantan have dropped significantly despite a rise in drug-related cases, says state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.
He said the decline suggested that efforts to curb cross-border smuggling were beginning to show results, with fewer drugs believed to be entering the state from neighbouring countries.
Yusoff said a new strategic approach to tackling the state's drug problem had been implemented since July 15, alongside sustained enforcement operations.
"Although the number of cases has increased, the supply of drugs into Kelantan has dropped significantly.
"We conduct operations daily, and despite the high number of operations, drug supplies are becoming increasingly limited.
"This indicates that drugs from neighbouring countries are no longer entering Kelantan as freely as before," he told reporters after a town hall discussion here.
He attributed the decline partly to tighter border controls introduced in 2024, which he said had helped curb illegal activities, including drug trafficking.
Yusoff said police would continue to strengthen enforcement and work with other agencies to tackle the drug problem more comprehensively.
On efforts to prevent drug abuse among students, he said the matter had been discussed with the relevant authorities.
He said he was informed that the Selangor Education Department had worked with the National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) to conduct urine tests on students.
However, he said it remained unclear whether the initiative could be extended nationwide, as police had yet to receive confirmation from the Education Ministry.
"Previously, we were instructed that students could not undergo urine tests. We will review the existing approach and examine whether the method used in Selangor can be adopted nationwide," he said.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said yesterday that four states — Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu — had
recorded drug involvement rates
above the national threshold.
Pendang in Kedah and Kuala Krai in Kelantan were the country's two highest-ranking districts, he said.
The figures were calculated based on the number of people involved in drug cases per 100,000 population, using an international standard adopted by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
